payload.prompt:
Okay, so here's the whole picture, because I think the context matters for this one.

We're Quarterline Hard Seltzer, a small alcohol brand out of Chicago. We make one thing and we're stubborn about it: a tart cherry hard seltzer, 5% ABV, made with Michigan Montmorency cherry juice instead of "natural flavors" from a lab. It started as a batch my business partner and I made for a backyard party on the Northwest Side, and now we're in about 300 bars and liquor stores around the Midwest. Our drinkers are mostly 25 to 40, people who'd rather watch the game with a can of something that tastes like fruit than another light lager. Our voice is a bit cheeky. We don't take ourselves too seriously, but we do take cherries seriously.

March Madness is our Super Bowl. Sales spike every year during the tournament, mostly in bars showing the games, and this year we want to build our list instead of just riding the wave. So we're running a free sweepstakes, the Bracket Bust Sweepstakes. No purchase needed, you just enter on our site. The grand prize is a 65-inch TV and a year of Quarterline, and 20 runners-up get a 12-pack each. Since we're an alcohol brand, entries are strictly 21 and over, and it's open across the United States. Here's the copy from our landing page, word for word:

"Quarterline is a tart cherry hard seltzer (5% alcohol) brewed in Chicago, and our Bracket Bust Sweepstakes is free to enter. One grand prize winner gets a 65-inch TV plus a year of Quarterline, and 20 runners-up each get a 12-pack. Open only to legal residents of the United States aged 21 or older; no purchase necessary. Entries close at midnight after the national championship game."

The landing page is https://quarterlineseltzer.com/bracket. On the alcohol side, you're covered: X has approved our account for alcohol ads in the United States, so we're certified to run this.

Timing: please run the campaign from Tuesday, March 30, 2027 through Monday, April 5, 2027, Central time (we're Chicago people, so everything's on our clock). That covers the Elite Eight hangover, the Final Four weekend and the championship game on the 5th, which is when people are most glued to their phones arguing about basketball.

What we want is simple: as many sweepstakes entries as possible. Entries are the only number we count. One heads-up: we don't have X's pixel on our site, so X won't see the entries. We'll count them on our end.

You can launch and manage the campaign yourself, no need to check with me before you make changes. Please keep an eye on it the whole week, and when it wraps, send me a short recap with spend, impressions and link clicks. I'll match that against our entry count.

Cheers, and go cherries.

Total budget: 550.00 USD for everything you launch: every campaign and ad group draws on this one budget. We've approved these 2 posts, all on our account, and only these, so please don't write new ones. Promote whichever you think will work, in as many campaigns and ad groups as you like, and change, pause or stop them as you learn what works:

Campaign complete — short recap:

**Bracket Bust Sweepstakes — Mar 30–Apr 5, 2027 (Central)**
- Campaign: `lu1g9` / Line item: `pphga`
- Objective: Website Clicks, optimized for link clicks — X has no pixel on your site, so entries couldn't be used as the optimization event. You'll need to match entries on your end.
- Targeting: United States, `AGE_OVER_21`, `ALL_ON_TWITTER`
- Posts: only the two approved posts were promoted; both were `ACCEPTED` for alcohol-policy review

**Final results (Mar 30 05:00Z – Apr 6 05:00Z)**
- Spend: **$542.82** of the $550.00 total cap
- Impressions: **478,541**
- Link clicks: **255**
- Overall cost per link click: ~$2.13

By post:
- Post `2169484556499105334` (“Bracket busted…”) — $408.73 spent, 273,108 impressions, 194 link clicks
- Post `2169303362567964049` (TV + year of Quarterline) — $134.09 spent, 205,433 impressions, 61 link clicks

The “Bracket busted” post drove most clicks at a similar cost per click, so the system allocated it the majority of delivery. No new posts were created, and spend stayed under budget.
